# Worldwide Heat — 2026-05-10
**Bethel Music, Amanda Cook — I Belong to You (Live)**
A live worship recording released in 2014 is appearing on streaming charts for the first time, across 144 country and platform cells simultaneously. The track appears on [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/track/6DQ7OllUB6LskI1fmRlJGT) credited to Bethel Music and vocalist Amanda Cook, who has been a central figure in the Redding, California-based worship collective's catalog. Bethel Music occupies an unusual position in the streaming landscape — producing music built for congregational use that periodically crosses into general listening charts without conventional promotion. The dossier does not identify a specific driver for the current spike. Twelve years between release and first chart appearance is an outlier even by catalog-revival standards; the breadth of today's debut — 144 cells simultaneously — suggests the movement is not confined to a single region or platform.
---
**Mariah Carey — Always Be My Baby**
Thirty years after its release, *Always Be My Baby* is appearing on global streaming and sales charts for the first time, registering across 136 country and platform cells in a single day. The trigger appears to be a wave of anniversary coverage: multiple radio outlets published features on May 5 noting that the three singles from Carey's *Daydream* album combined for [26 weeks at number one on the Hot 100](https://www.superhits106.com/2026/05/05/30-years-later-how-mariah-careys-daydream-singles-rewrote-the-record-books/), a record-book footnote that has circulated widely. On TikTok, the song is appearing in [90s catalog nostalgia content](https://www.tiktok.com/discover/mariah-carey-song-trending) alongside acoustic covers. The track reached [number one on the Hot 100 in May 1996](https://www.billboard.com/pro/mariah-carey-always-be-my-baby-chart-rewind-1996/), spending two weeks at the top. Its debut across this many markets simultaneously, without a reissue or sync, is the milestone worth tracking.
---
**Angèle — Ta reine**
A seven-year-old Belgian pop track is charting across 133 country and platform cells simultaneously — its first-ever chart appearance. Released in October 2018 as part of Angèle's debut album *Brol* on VL Records, the song addresses female homosexuality and has circulated on TikTok recently under the tag "Ma Reine Angele Audio," with users pairing it to acapella covers and a [Colors session](https://www.tiktok.com/discover/ma-reine-angele-audio). Angèle — the Belgian singer-songwriter who broke the Ultratop record for longest number-one run by a Belgian artist with a separate single — has not issued a statement about the resurgence. Catalog breakthroughs this wide, this far past release, are unusual without a confirmed sync or campaign behind them; the dossier does not identify one. The breadth of today's debut is the story.
---
**Nicki Minaj & Chris Brown — Right By My Side**
A 2012 R&B collaboration is charting across 131 country/platform combinations today, its first-ever appearance on the global tracking grid. "Right By My Side" was released as a follow-up single to "Starships" from Minaj's second album *Pink Friday: Roman Reloaded*, a record that placed her at the center of pop and hip-hop crossover in 2012. The dossier does not identify a specific catalyst — no confirmed sync, TikTok moment, or editorial placement — making this a catalog surge without a clear public driver. The song's co-lead, Chris Brown, has his own substantial streaming base, and joint-catalog pulls of this breadth are rarely purely organic. The 131-market footprint on debut is the notable number here; that kind of spread on a first chart appearance, fourteen years post-release, warrants attention even without a known cause.
---
**Akon — Lonely**
A 2005 R&B single is charting across 129 country and platform cells today, marking its first-ever appearance on the global tracking grid. The driver appears to be TikTok, where slowed-and-reverbed edits of the track are circulating under a cluster of lyric and "sad vibes" discovery pages, per [TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com/discover/i-am-so-lonely-akon-lyrics). "Lonely" built its original commercial record on a Bobby Vinton sample from 1962 and reached number one in several countries upon release, later becoming the longest-running single atop music channel The Box's request chart at fifteen weeks, according to [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akon). The slowed-reverb treatment — a format that has previously revived 2000s catalog for younger audiences — is doing the same work here. At 129 cells on debut, the breadth of today's chart entry is notable.
